class.name: PhysXFlowSimulation3D
class.brief_description: A NVIDIA Flow sparse-grid fluid/fire/smoke simulation (Flow 2.2), provided by the PhysX module.
class.description: Runs NVIDIA Flow (the realtime sparse-voxel combustion solver that ships alongside PhysX, loaded at runtime from [code]nvflow.dll[/code]/[code]nvflowext.dll[/code]) on its own GPU device -- Flow is architecturally a sibling of PhysX and Blast, not a physics subsystem; this node simply steps it from the scene tree's physics tick. Unlike a fixed-domain volume, a Flow grid is [b]sparse and unbounded[/b]: blocks allocate anywhere emitters touch, bounded only by [member max_blocks]. Author with [PhysXFlowEmitter3D] nodes (list their paths in [member emitters]) and colliders in [member colliders]: explicit [PhysXFlowCollider3D] nodes, or any physics body (StaticBody3D / RigidBody3D / kinematic bodies -- their server-side transform, velocity and shape data are consumed directly, with triangle-mesh collision for concave shapes and moving-body velocity coupling). Combustion is real: emitters inject temperature/fuel/smoke channels; fuel above the ignition temperature burns, raising temperature further (rising fireball), generating smoke and cooling over time. Pure smoke emitters set temperature/fuel to 0. Renders through a stock FogVolume fed by a readback of the sparse volume (smoke density shades as fog; the solver's colorized fire channels add emission). Requires the Forward+ renderer for visuals; the simulation itself runs regardless (headless included). Flow runs on its own GPU backend selected by [code]physics/physx_3d/flow/device_api[/code]; without a usable device every node reports unavailable and stays inert -- scenes load and run, only without Flow effects. [b]Known v1 limits:[/b] collision meshes rebuild when a body's shape changes are not yet diffed (a changed shape resource gets a fresh cache entry automatically, since meshes are cached per shape RID); the CPU-side readback decode costs roughly 0.5-8 ms per step depending on plume size (measured), which large scenes may want to reduce by raising [member cell_size].

method.name: add_transient_emitter
method.description: Spawns a one-shot world-space emitter (a puff) that decays over [param lifetime] seconds of simulated time. This is the generic event-adapter target: [PhysXFlowBlastBridge3D] forwards destruction events here, and scripts may call it for impacts, explosions, torches, etc. The puff spreads as it fades.

method.name: get_active_block_count
method.description: Number of sparse blocks currently allocated by the solver.

method.name: get_active_bounds_min
method.description: World-space minimum corner of the last decoded volume (the active plume's bounding box). Zero until the first readback completes.

method.name: get_active_bounds_size
method.description: World-space size of the last decoded volume. Zero until the first readback completes.

method.name: get_diagnostics
method.description: Live diagnostics: [code]available[/code], [code]unavailable_reason[/code], [code]backend[/code] ("vulkan"/"cpu"), [code]simulations[/code], [code]active_blocks[/code], [member max_blocks], [code]frames_simulated[/code], [code]sim_time[/code], [code]device_memory_mb[/code], [code]readback_memory_mb[/code], and the last step's CPU timings in microseconds ([code]last_submit_usec[/code], [code]last_flush_usec[/code], [code]last_decode_usec[/code]).

method.name: get_last_max_smoke
method.description: Highest smoke density in the last decoded frame. 0 means "genuinely nothing in the volume" (or no readback yet) -- the quickest way to tell an empty simulation from a rendering problem.

method.name: get_last_max_temperature
method.description: Highest temperature in the last decoded frame.

method.name: is_flow_available
method.description: True when the shared Flow runtime initialized successfully (a GPU/CPU device was created and nvflow.dll loaded). False means the node is inert; see [method get_diagnostics] for the reason.

method.name: reset_simulation
method.description: Clears the sparse grid (all allocated blocks, all channels) and restarts the simulation clock. Transient emitters are dropped.

method.name: step_once
method.description: Advances exactly one 1/60 s step while [member paused]. No effect while unpaused (the simulation already steps every tick).

members.member: Seconds an inactive sparse block stays allocated before being reclaimed (hysteresis against flicker).
Additional buoyancy per unit smoke density.
Upward force per unit temperature (drives plume rise).
Voxel edge in meters. 0 requests the SDK's auto cell size, which currently fails to allocate without a seeded size (measured on Flow 2.2.0) -- prefer a real value.
Half-extent used for [member colliders] entries that resolve to a plain Node3D.
NodePaths to colliders: [PhysXFlowCollider3D] nodes, physics bodies (server-side shape/transform/velocity consumed directly), or standalone CollisionShape3D nodes.
Toggles the fuel-burn-temperature-smoke reaction; off = pure advected smoke.
Exponential temperature cooling rate.

Copies the gas back to the CPU once every few steps for the query API ([method get_last_max_smoke], bounds). The GPU render path never touches it; only turn this off if you read none of the query values.
Prints per-step sparse layout and readback statistics to the console (diagnostics only).
NodePaths to [PhysXFlowEmitter3D] nodes (any other Node3D becomes a default smoke sphere at its position, aimed by its orientation).
Disabling also resets the simulation.
Emits light from the solver's colorized fire channels (RGB of the readback volume).
Emission intensity scale.

With this on, gas never goes below [member floor_height]: one wide solid under the grid (a solid reserves no blocks, so it costs nothing). Colliders cannot describe terrain, so without a floor a blast's or a fire's gas sinks into the ground and spends the grid's block budget there.
The world-space Y the [member floor_enabled] solid's top sits at.
Fog density multiplier applied to the smoke channel.
Fuel dissipation per second.
Buoyancy reference gravity inside the solver (Flow's own units; [member buoyancy_per_temp] works against this). Redot's world gravity does not automatically apply -- a Flow volume is its own world.
Sparse block budget (allocation cap). Changing it recreates the grid (clears the simulation).
Catch-up cap: at most this many solver steps per engine tick, so a hitch cannot stall the frame.
Freezes the solver (existing density keeps rendering). Combine with [member simulate_when_paused] or [method step_once] for scrubbing workflows.
Pressure projection (divergence-free velocity). Off is cheaper but lets emitters push through walls.
